description: Show orchestrator token spend on the cam dashboard (and cam status), parsed from the Claude Code transcript JSONL with honest cached vs fresh breakdown.

userStories.title: Deduplicate transcript usage lines before summing
userStories.description: As the dashboard and cam status token row, I need parseTranscriptUsage to dedupe usage entries by request before summing, because real Claude Code transcripts write one JSONL line per content block (all carrying the same usage object), so naive summing inflates the displayed totals 2x to 5x and breaks the feature's honest-numbers contract.
acceptanceCriteria: [src/transcript/usage.ts:47-79] parseTranscriptUsage no longer sums every line that carries message.usage. Real Claude Code transcripts write multiple JSONL lines per assistant turn (one per content block: thinking, text, tool_use), each carrying an IDENTICAL message.usage object, so naive summation inflates totals 2x to 5x (verified empirically on ~/.claude/projects in review round 2: 91 unique message ids across 181 occurrences in one transcript; one msg id appearing 5x with identical usage in another). Dedupe before summing: key each usage-bearing line by (message.id, requestId) (verify the exact top-level field names empirically against a real transcript before coding), keep the final usage payload per key, then sum the deduped set. Lines that carry message.usage but lack a dedup key fall back to being counted once each (no collision).

test/transcript/usage.test.ts gains a fixture where the same (message.id, requestId) repeats across multiple lines with identical usage, asserting the request is counted ONCE not N times; the existing distinct-line sum assertions stay green.
bun run typecheck passes
bun test passes
userStories.notes: Review round 2 finding (CRITICAL). Core correctness of the CAM-21 honest-numbers contract: the rendered row (renderTokensLine) is laid out correctly but the underlying totals are inflated, which is worse than omitting the row. Dedup strategy matches ccusage and claude-devtools (key by message.id + requestId, keep last usage per request). Sources: gille.ai/en/blog/claude-code-jsonl-logs-undercount-tokens, github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/5034, github.com/matt1398/claude-devtools/issues/74, ccusage.com/api/data-loader. Triaged to backlog/skip (do NOT implement here): the WARNING on shell-injection via genSessionId (run.ts:155, production uses randomUUID so the value is always clean hex) and the two SUGGESTIONS (.gitignore .claude/.cam-*, stories field absent from snapshotKey, both pre-existing/out-of-scope). Conventional commit: fix: US-R2-001 - dedupe transcript usage lines before summing.

userStories.title: Include cache token fields in dashboard snapshotKey
userStories.description: As the legacy non-Ink dashboard render loop, I need snapshotKey to hash all four token fields so a poll where only cache totals change still triggers a redraw, matching the US-003 acceptance criterion that snapshotKey incorporates token totals.
acceptanceCriteria: [src/commands/dashboard.ts:701-716] snapshotKey appends `data.tokensCacheRead ?? -1` and `data.tokensCacheCreation ?? -1` to the hashed array, alongside the existing `tokensInput`/`tokensOutput` entries, so all four token fields contribute to the snapshot identity (US-003 AC: 'snapshotKey incorporates token totals so the legacy non-Ink loop redraws when tokens change' — currently only 2 of 4 are honored, found in review round 1).
bun run typecheck passes
bun test passes
userStories.notes: Review round 1 finding (WARNING). Mechanical, single-file. The displayed tokens line (renderTokensLine) uses in = input + cacheCreation + cacheRead and cached = cacheRead, so cache fields are load-bearing for the rendered string; the legacy loop must redraw when they change. Production path is Ink (re-renders via setState every poll) so impact is bounded to the non-Ink loop, but the AC is literal. Conventional commit: fix: US-R1-001 - include cache token fields in dashboard snapshotKey.

userStories.title: Pure transcript-usage parser + formatTokens
userStories.description: As the dashboard renderer, I need a pure parser that sums token usage across a Claude Code transcript JSONL plus a compact number formatter, so downstream stories can render orchestrator spend without re-deriving the wire format.
acceptanceCriteria: New module src/transcript/usage.ts exports parseTranscriptUsage(jsonl: string) that returns { input, output, cacheRead, cacheCreation } summed across every line whose parsed JSON has message.usage (assistant or sidechain), skipping malformed JSON lines and lines without message.usage silently.
New helper formatTokens(n: number): string in the same module renders 1234567 as '1.2M', 340000 as '340k', 999 as '999' (round to 1 decimal for M, integer for k, raw for <1000; 0 renders as '0').

New test file test/transcript/usage.test.ts covers: (a) a multi-line fixture with two assistant lines + one isSidechain assistant line + one malformed line + one non-assistant line, asserting the four summed totals; (b) formatTokens for the three magnitudes plus 0 and an edge value just under each threshold.
bun run typecheck passes
bun test passes
userStories.notes: Files: src/transcript/usage.ts (new), test/transcript/usage.test.ts (new). Wire shape (verified empirically): each line of the transcript JSONL is one JSON object; the assistant entries that carry token accounting have shape { type:'assistant', sessionId, isSidechain?:boolean, message:{ usage:{ input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, ... } } }. Sum across ALL lines with message.usage (including isSidechain:true Task subagents) since that is the true orchestrator-session total. Skip malformed/non-JSON lines silently (best-effort, never throw). Codebase patterns: noUncheckedIndexedAccess is on, so guard array/object access (split-by-newline returns string[] but indexing into JSON.parse results needs runtime shape checks). This module is pure (no I/O), so Node/Bun runtime parity is not a concern: prefer plain JSON.parse + string.split('\n'). Conventional commit: feat: US-001 - parse Claude Code transcript usage.

userStories.title: Capture orchestrator session id in cam run + transcript path resolver
userStories.description: As the dashboard, I need cam run to start the orchestrator with a known session id (written to a marker file) and a helper that resolves the transcript path, so I can locate the JSONL that holds the orchestrator's usage.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/run.ts: RunOptions gains an optional genSessionId?: () => string (default = randomUUID from node:crypto). setupOrchestratorSession generates a uuid via that function, passes --session-id <uuid> to the claude orchestrator invocation (the existing claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions ... command in pane 0), and writes the uuid to .claude/.cam-orch-session (utf8).

On session RE-ATTACH (ensureProjectSession returns false → setupOrchestratorSession returns { created: false }) the marker file is NOT rewritten, so the original orchestrator session id persists across cam run invocations.

src/transcript/usage.ts (or sibling) exports orchestratorTranscriptPath(cwd: string, claudeDir: string): string | null that reads .claude/.cam-orch-session from cwd and returns <claudeDir>/projects/<encode(cwd)>/<uuid>.jsonl, where encode replaces every char not matching /[a-zA-Z0-9]/ with '-' (verified empirically). claudeDir MUST be resolved by callers as (process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? join(os.homedir(), '.claude')): Claude Code honors CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for the projects/ transcript root (confirmed in official docs), and the operator runs with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-pessoal, so hardcoding ~/.claude reads the wrong directory and tokens come back zero (US-005 would fail while unit tests pass). The .claude/.cam-orch-session marker stays in cwd/.claude (the project dir), which is unrelated to CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Returns null when the marker file is absent or empty.

test/run.test.ts: the existing 'respawns the claude command in pane 0' test (or an equivalent one asserting the orchestrator argv) now asserts --session-id <fixed-uuid> is present in the respawn-pane argv AND that .claude/.cam-orch-session exists with that uuid as its content; the test injects a deterministic genSessionId returning a fixed string.

New test coverage for orchestratorTranscriptPath under test/transcript/: encoding, null-when-missing-marker, AND a test asserting it honors an injected claudeDir (e.g. a tmpdir standing in for CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR) rather than hardcoding ~/.claude.
bun run typecheck passes
bun test passes
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/run.ts (modify setupOrchestratorSession + RunOptions), src/transcript/usage.ts (add orchestratorTranscriptPath), test/run.test.ts (extend existing assertions), test/transcript/usage.test.ts or a new file under test/transcript/ (new coverage for the resolver). The agentCmd string in run.ts is the surface to patch: today it is `claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions "$(cat '${promptFile}')"; tmux -L cam kill-session ...`; insert `--session-id <uuid>` between bypassPermissions and the prompt. Use randomUUID from node:crypto (matches the file's existing node: idiom: this file already uses node:fs, node:child_process, node:path). The --session-id flag is documented in `claude --help` as 'Use a specific session ID for the conversation' (verified externally, not a fetchable doc URL — note in officialDocsValidated when filing handoff, but the PRD officialDocsConsulted stays []). Encoding rule (verified against ~/.claude/projects): cwd.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, '-'). Inject `home` (not hardcode os.homedir()) so the resolver is testable against a tmpdir. Re-attach guard MUST live in setupOrchestratorSession's early-return path: the marker write happens AFTER `if (!panes) return { created: false }` so re-attach is a no-op for the marker. Codebase patterns: noUncheckedIndexedAccess (guard the readFileSync result + trim before returning). Conventional commit: feat: US-002 - capture orchestrator session id and resolve transcript path.

userStories.title: Surface orchestrator tokens in the dashboard
userStories.description: As the operator watching cam dashboard, I want to see how many tokens the orchestrator has spent, refreshed live, so I know if the session is burning context or sitting idle.
acceptanceCriteria: src/commands/dashboard.ts: DashboardData gains optional token fields { tokensInput?: number; tokensOutput?: number; tokensCacheRead?: number; tokensCacheCreation?: number } (cache fields added now to keep US-004's diff small).

readSnapshot best-effort reads .claude/.cam-orch-session via orchestratorTranscriptPath, reads the JSONL (via existsSync + readFileSync, matching the existing node:fs idiom in this file), and calls parseTranscriptUsage; on any miss (no marker / no transcript file / read error) the token fields stay undefined and rendering omits the row. readSnapshot never throws.

readSnapshot accepts an injectable claudeDir option (default process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? join(os.homedir(), '.claude')) so tests can point at a tmpdir; the option is plumbed through runDashboard / runDashboardInk so the Ink path stays testable.
snapshotKey now incorporates the token totals so the legacy non-Ink render loop redraws when tokens change.

src/ui/Dashboard.tsx SummaryPanel renders a new SummaryRow label='tokens' inside the Loop Section that prints '<in> in · <out> out' using formatTokens (e.g. '1.2M in · 340k out'), where in = tokensInput + tokensCacheCreation + tokensCacheRead (total input volume, not just the non-cached portion; US-004 adds the cached breakdown). When tokensInput is undefined, the row is omitted (do not render placeholder dashes; keep the Loop section compact in the ~36-col cam run pane).

Test coverage: a readSnapshot test that writes a fixture .claude/.cam-orch-session + a fixture transcript JSONL under an injected home tmpdir and asserts the four token fields populate; a second test for the missing-marker path asserting fields stay undefined and no throw.
bun run typecheck passes
bun test passes
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/dashboard.ts (extend DashboardData, readSnapshot, snapshotKey, RunDashboardOptions, RunDashboardInkOptions), src/ui/Dashboard.tsx (add the tokens SummaryRow), test/dashboard.test.ts or sibling (new coverage). Match the existing file idiom: dashboard.ts already imports node:fs, node:path, node:child_process — keep that style, do not introduce Bun.file mid-file. The Loop Section in Dashboard.tsx is the SummaryPanel render starting at the `<Section heading="Loop" ...>` block; insert the tokens row after `since` and before `branch` (keeps state/story/progress/iter/since at the top, tokens + branch at the bottom). The cam run dashboard pane is ~36 cols wide (split layout); '1.2M in · 340k out' fits in ~22 cols including the muted label column. Codebase patterns: noUncheckedIndexedAccess (parseTranscriptUsage return is { input, output, cacheRead, cacheCreation }, destructure carefully), readSnapshot is read-only (never throw — wrap every IO in try/catch and fall through to defaults — see the existing readPrd/readState pattern in this same file for shape). Conventional commit: feat: US-003 - surface orchestrator tokens in dashboard.

userStories.title: Cached-token honesty in dashboard + cam status parity
userStories.description: As the operator, I want the token row to clearly separate fresh input from cached input so a cache-dominated total is not misread as fresh spend, and I want the same row on cam status so the print path matches the dashboard.
acceptanceCriteria: src/ui/Dashboard.tsx tokens SummaryRow now renders '<in> in (<cached> cached) · <out> out' where in = tokensInput + tokensCacheCreation + tokensCacheRead (total input volume) and cached = tokensCacheRead only, using formatTokens for all three magnitudes. cache_creation is fresh spend (billed above the base input rate), so it MUST stay folded into the in total and MUST NOT be counted as cached, otherwise the '(cached)' label understates real spend (Honest Numbers). When cached is 0 the '(0 cached)' suffix is omitted (clean display for runs with no cache yet); when cached > 0 it always appears, even if tiny.

src/commands/status.ts: StatusReport gains an optional tokens?: { input: number; output: number; cacheRead: number; cacheCreation: number }. buildStatusReport resolves the transcript via orchestratorTranscriptPath using the same injectable claudeDir option pattern added in US-003 (extend StatusOptions with claudeDir?: string defaulting to process.env.CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ?? join(os.homedir(), '.claude')), and populates tokens when both marker and transcript are present; otherwise leaves it undefined.

runStatus renders a `tokens` entry via renderEntry under the Loop section (after `last`, before `promise`) using the same wording as the dashboard: '<in> in (<cached> cached) · <out> out', omitting the cached suffix when 0. The row is skipped entirely when report.tokens is undefined (no orchestrator transcript available).

Test coverage: extend the existing dashboard render assertion (or add one) to confirm the cached suffix appears when cache totals are non-zero and is omitted when zero; extend buildStatusReport tests (or add one) to assert tokens populates from a fixture transcript and is undefined when the marker is missing.

Wording must match exactly between Dashboard.tsx and status.ts (single source of truth: a small renderTokensLine(t) helper in src/transcript/usage.ts that both consumers import keeps the strings aligned). renderTokensLine computes in = t.input + t.cacheCreation + t.cacheRead and cached = t.cacheRead (cache_creation is fresh, never counted as cached), so the honest in/cached split lives in one place and cannot drift between the two surfaces.
bun run typecheck passes
bun test passes
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/status.ts (extend StatusReport, buildStatusReport, runStatus, StatusOptions), src/ui/Dashboard.tsx (update the tokens row text), src/transcript/usage.ts (add renderTokensLine helper for the shared format string), test/status.test.ts + test/dashboard.test.ts (extend). status.ts already uses node:fs / node:path / node:child_process — keep that idiom. The renderTokensLine helper avoids the two surfaces drifting on cache wording (Eduardo's CLAUDE.md §7 Doc Maintenance: 'if I move behaviour I document, I update doc in the same edit' — the symmetric rule for code: if two surfaces show the same number, they share one renderer). Sample numbers from the issue (cache_read 450k, fresh input 22k) drove the design decision: the cached portion is the dominant share of real usage so it must be visible. Codebase patterns: in Ink, success/failure is the glyph (✓/✗) and the row is a SummaryRow inside the Loop Section, so no divider color change is needed. Conventional commit: feat: US-004 - show cached token breakdown and propagate to cam status.

userStories.title: Operator smoke: real cam run shows non-zero tokens
userStories.description: As the operator, I confirm in a real terminal that cam run boots the orchestrator with the new --session-id flag, writes the marker, and that after a few orchestrator turns the dashboard + cam status show a non-zero, well-formatted tokens row.
acceptanceCriteria: Operator runs `cam run` in a real terminal against a project where cam-cli is installed; the orchestrator pane boots cleanly (no regression vs the pre-CAM-21 behaviour: claude greets the operator, prompt loads, no error spew).

Operator confirms .claude/.cam-orch-session was written and contains a valid uuid; the transcript JSONL exists at <claudeDir>/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<uuid>.jsonl after the first orchestrator turn, where claudeDir = $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR if set else ~/.claude (on the operator's machine this resolves to ~/.claude-pessoal).
After a few orchestrator turns, the dashboard Loop section shows a non-zero `tokens` row formatted as '<in> in (<cached> cached) · <out> out' (or without the cached suffix if cache is 0).
`cam status` from a second terminal shows the matching `tokens` row under Loop, with the same wording as the dashboard.

Operator captures any drift (e.g. row truncated in the narrow pane, label alignment off, formatTokens edge cases) as a note in the handoff for a follow-up story; passes:true only after visual confirmation.
userStories.notes: This is the visual + real-boot ceremony stories US-001..004 cannot cover from unit tests alone (autonomous implementer cannot launch a real claude session and observe its transcript). Operator-only; the autonomous loop will skip this story (per scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md § Stop Condition: requires:operator stories are out-of-scope for autonomous implementation, the operator flips passes:true after the ceremony). No quality-gate ACs (typecheck/test) because there is no code to land in this story: the implementer ahead of it already shipped + verified static gates. Reference real wire numbers from the issue (cache_read 450k vs fresh input 22k) to validate the cached-honesty wording reads correctly with a cache-dominated total.
